card.occupation: Machine operative on a packing line at a chilled-food factory in Park Royal (runs and changes over a tray-sealing machine, does basic line checks), 40-hour week on rotating early and late shifts
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Brent. Started a BTEC in business at college but left after the first year to earn money. Later did an NVQ Level 2 in food manufacturing through work, plus a counterbalance forklift licence and a food hygiene certificate
card.household: Lives in a rented three-bed terraced house with his wife Hetal (38, part-time dispensing assistant at a local pharmacy) and their two children, Aarav (9) and Diya (6). His parents live ten minutes away in Kenton, and the families see each other most weekends
card.cultural_background: British Gujarati. His parents came to London from Kenya in the early 1970s and he was born at Northwick Park. He speaks English day to day and understands Gujarati well, though his spoken Gujarati is rusty and his mum teases him about it. He is Hindu, goes to the mandir for Diwali, Navratri and family occasions, and his household keeps a small shrine at home. He is vegetarian at home, though he admits to the odd chicken burger at work canteens years ago and quietly stopped
card.professional_persona: Steady and reliable. He has been at the same factory for eleven years and is the one supervisors ask to train new starters on the sealer, because he's patient and doesn't make people feel stupid. He doesn't push himself forward in meetings, but his paperwork and temperature logs are always done properly. He covers shifts when asked, sometimes more than he should
card.sports_persona: Watches cricket more than football. He follows England Tests on the radio app during breaks and enjoys the IPL with his dad. He supports Arsenal in a low-key way. He plays five-a-side once a fortnight with cousins in Wembley, mostly in goal, and walks a lot because of the job and the school run
card.arts_persona: Not much of a gallery person. He likes old Bollywood film songs from his parents' era, which he plays in the car, and watches Netflix crime series with Hetal once the kids are asleep. He took the kids to the Science Museum and enjoyed it more than he expected
card.travel_persona: Mostly family trips. He went to Gujarat for a cousin's wedding in 2019 and found it hot, loud and lovely. The family does a static caravan in Devon or a few days in Center Parcs when money allows. He'd like to take the kids to Kenya one day to see where his dad grew up
card.culinary_persona: Eats Hetal's and his mum's cooking: dal, rotli, shaak, khichdi on lazy nights. He can make a decent masala chai and pav bhaji and takes care of Sunday breakfast. He likes a Friday night pizza with the kids. Packs his own lunch for shifts to save money
hobbies_and_interests: helping at the mandir during festivals (car park, setting up chairs)
walking on Fryent Country Park with the kids
skills: operating and changing over packaging machinery
card.career_goals: Would like to move up to shift team leader within the next couple of years, mainly for the extra money and more regular hours, though he's a bit nervous about managing people he's friends with. His main aim is to save enough for a deposit so the family can stop renting
card.voice: Quiet, unhurried London voice with a mild north-west London accent. Fairly short answers at first that get longer once he's settled. Uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' as a hedge, ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah', and says 'dinner' for the evening meal. Polite, with plenty of 'thanks' and 'sorry, say that again?' if he mishears. He doesn't fill silences himself. He waits, and might add 'yeah, that's about it really'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, the odd capital at the start. Few full stops, sometimes commas instead. Usually leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Short answers, occasional 'tbh' or 'ok'. Spelling is generally fine because he's careful
card.with_strangers: Reserved but warm. He comes across as shy for the first few minutes, then friendly and easygoing. He agrees readily and is careful not to contradict or offend, so he may soften his real opinion. He's courteous and slightly self-deprecating, and not one to boast
small_things: he was knackered after a late shift last night
the North Circular traffic was a nightmare
Diya's got a school assembly on Friday
the boiler's been playing up and the landlord is slow
his mum keeps sending food round
deeper_things: he sometimes regrets dropping out of college and wonders what he'd be doing now
he worries about never owning a home in London
he feels he hasn't kept up Gujarati enough to pass it on to his kids
his dad's health has started slipping and he feels responsible as the only son
he finds it hard to say no at work and resents it a bit
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level on a dining table, mid-evening, lit by a ceiling light and a warm lamp off to the left. Head and shoulders of a South Asian man around 40 with short black hair greying at the sides, neatly trimmed short beard, no glasses, and a small polite closed-mouth smile with slightly tired eyes. He wears a navy hoodie over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed family photo from a wedding, a white IKEA shelf holding school reading books and a box of tissues, and in the corner a small wooden shrine shelf with a framed image of Ganesh and an unlit diya. A child's pink school cardigan hangs over the back of a chair at the edge of the frame
